results.corrected_claim:
Declaration (verbatim): `nonisolated func onHingeChange(isEnabled: Bool = true, _ action: @escaping (DeviceHingeContext, DeviceHingeContext) -> Void) -> some View`. Abstract: "Adds an action to perform when the hinge context of the view hierarchy changes."
- `struct DeviceHingeContext` has `var hinge: DeviceHinge?` ("The current hinge of the device.").
- `struct DeviceHinge` has `var angle: Angle` and `var status: DeviceHinge.Status`.
- `DeviceHinge.Status` is a struct, not an enum. Its members are `static var closed`, `static var partiallyOpen` and `static var fullyOpen`.
- Availability is 27.1 everywhere, but only iOS and iPadOS 27.1 are flagged beta. Mac Catalyst, macOS, tvOS, visionOS and watchOS list 27.1 with no beta flag, so "All BETA 27.1" in correct_info is loose; the finding's availability field is exact.
- The SwiftUI Updates page (September 2026, heading "Hinge") says: "Observe changes to the state of the hinge on iPhone Duo using the onHingeChange(isEnabled:_:) modifier, which delivers updates through DeviceHingeContext."
results.notes:
Sources (all apple-doc): DocC JSON for view/onhingechange(isenabled:_:), devicehingecontext, devicehinge, devicehinge/status-swift.struct, and updates/swiftui (September 2026 section).
- The overview text on DeviceHinge and DeviceHingeContext calls the modifier `onHingeChange(_:)`, which is inconsistent with the real symbol `onHingeChange(isEnabled:_:)`.
- Because Status is a struct with static members, a `switch` over it needs a `default` case.
- The doc sample uses `.onHingeChange { _, newContext in hinge = newContext.hinge }`.
- Related lead: the same September 2026 section adds "Reserved regions" (`ReservedRegion`, `reservedRegions(kind:options:layoutDirectionBehavior:)`) for avoiding the camera and hinge areas.
- The iOS 27 release notes do not mention the hinge.

results.corrected_claim:
Declaration (verbatim, iOS 27.0 and iPadOS 27.0, not beta): `nonisolated func sceneAccessory<C>(@ContentBuilder content: () -> C) -> some View where C : SceneAccessoryContent`.
- `SceneAccessoryContent` is a `@MainActor protocol` (iOS/iPadOS 27.0). It provides `func onAvailabilityChange(perform: (Bool) -> Void) -> some SceneAccessoryContent`, which both accessories get through conformance.
- `nonisolated struct ExternalNonInteractiveAccessory<Content> where Content : View` is iOS/iPadOS 27.0. Abstract: "A scene accessory that presents non-interactive content on an external display." It can also present over AirPlay.
- `nonisolated struct CameraCaptureAccessory<Content> where Content : View` is iOS/iPadOS 27.1, beta. Abstract: "A scene accessory that presents content during camera capture." Unlike the external accessory, its content can be interactive.
- Both accessories have `init(content: () -> Content)` and `init(isEnabled: Binding<Bool>, content: () -> Content)`.
- The "iPhone Duo outer display" detail comes from the SwiftUI Updates page (September 2026, "Scene accessories"), not from the symbol page: "Present content on the outer display of iPhone Duo while the device is open, the app is in the foreground, and a camera capture session is active, using CameraCaptureAccessory."
results.notes:
Sources: DocC JSON for view/sceneaccessory(content:), sceneaccessorycontent, externalnoninteractiveaccessory, cameracaptureaccessory and updates/swiftui (apple-doc), plus the iOS & iPadOS 27 release notes (apple-other).
- Release note 175548901: "In apps built with the iOS 27.0 SDK, you can display non-interactive content on external display scenes using the `.sceneAccessory` view modifier with an `ExternalNonInteractiveAccessory` type."
- Related UIKit behaviour change, note 177015874: apps built with the iOS 27.0 SDK no longer get `windowExternalDisplayNonInteractive` scenes automatically.
- The declarations also list Mac Catalyst, but the availability metadata lists only iOS and iPadOS.
- These APIs are not specific to Liquid Glass.

results.corrected_claim:
`typealias ContentBuilder = ViewBuilder`. Docs list availability iOS 13.0, iPadOS 13.0, Mac Catalyst 13.0, macOS 10.15, tvOS 13.0, visionOS 1.0, watchOS 6.0, and the discussion calls it "the unified replacement for type-specific builders like ToolbarContentBuilder and CommandsBuilder".

Apple's current declarations print `@ContentBuilder` in every case checked (verbatim):
- `@MainActor @preconcurrency init(spacing: CGFloat? = nil, @ContentBuilder content: () -> Content)` on GlassEffectContainer
- `tabViewBottomAccessory<Content>(@ContentBuilder content:)` and `tabViewBottomAccessory(isEnabled:@ContentBuilder content:)`
- `safeAreaBar(edge:alignment:spacing:@ContentBuilder content:)`
- `ToolbarOverflowMenu`'s `nonisolated init(@ContentBuilder content: () -> Content)` (it is a struct, iOS 27.0, not a `toolbarOverflowMenu` modifier)
- `swipeActions(edge:allowsFullSwipe:@ContentBuilder content:)`
- every `alert(_:isPresented:actions:message:)` overload, with `@ContentBuilder` on both `actions` and `message`

Because it is a typealias, existing `@ViewBuilder` code still compiles, and ViewBuilder is not marked deprecated. Naming `ContentBuilder` in source needs the Xcode 27 SDK.

In the skill, only references/01-api-reference.md lines 116–117 use `@ViewBuilder` in signatures, so "throughout" overstates it. The `@ViewBuilder` uses in the examples are on computed properties or functions and remain valid. Apple documents a single GlassEffectContainer initializer, `init(spacing:content:)` with spacing defaulting to nil, so the separate `init(@ViewBuilder content:)` listed at line 116 is not a distinct documented overload.
results.notes:
Sources (apple-doc unless noted): DocC JSON for contentbuilder, viewbuilder, glasseffectcontainer, glasseffectcontainer/init(spacing:content:), view/tabviewbottomaccessory(content:), view/tabviewbottomaccessory(isenabled:content:), view/safeareabar(edge:alignment:spacing:content:), toolbaroverflowmenu/init(content:), view/swipeactions(edge:allowsfullswipe:content:), view/alert(_:ispresented:actions:message:), and updates/swiftui (June 2026, General).
- The ViewBuilder page says: "When you build your project in Xcode 26 and earlier, use ViewBuilder..." and "When you build in Xcode 27 and later for any version of SwiftUI, the system constructs type-agnostic content from ViewBuilder closures... Mark closures with the type alias ContentBuilder instead to indicate where your code expects this behavior."
- Skill code that must still build with Xcode 26 should keep `@ViewBuilder`.
- Release note 177526032 (apple-other) mentions improved `@ContentBuilder` type-checking performance.
- Side note: the GlassEffectContainer page lists iOS, iPadOS, Mac Catalyst, macOS, tvOS and watchOS 26.0, and no visionOS.

results.corrected_claim:
The new API is correct. `static var statusBar: ToolbarPlacement { get }` is iOS 27.0, iPadOS 27.0 and Mac Catalyst 27.0, abstract "The system status bar." The discussion matches verbatim: "Use with toolbarVisibility(_:for:) to hide the status bar, or with toolbarColorScheme(_:for:) to specify the preferred status bar style." and "Using this placement with other toolbar customization APIs has no effect." The doc sample is `.toolbarVisibility(hideStatusBar ? .hidden : .automatic, for: .statusBar).toolbarColorScheme(.dark, for: .statusBar)`.

The premise is wrong for visibility. SwiftUI has had `statusBarHidden(_:)` since iOS 13: `@export(implementation) nonisolated func statusBarHidden(_ hidden: Bool = true) -> some View`. It now carries deprecatedAt 27.2 on iOS, iPadOS and Mac Catalyst with the message "Use .toolbarVisibility(_, for: .statusBar) instead". On visionOS it is also deprecatedAt 27.2, with the message "Has no effect on visionOS".

What iOS 27 really adds is a SwiftUI status-bar style control plus one unified placement for both visibility and style. The skill's examples/04-PhotoDetailScreen.swift does not handle the status bar at all; it only has `.preferredColorScheme(.dark)` at line 88.
results.notes:
Sources: DocC JSON for toolbarplacement/statusbar and view/statusbarhidden(_:) (apple-doc), plus the iOS & iPadOS 27 release notes (apple-other).
- Release note 165329279: "You can use `.toolbarVisibility(hideStatusBar ? .hidden : .automatic, for: .statusBar)` to conditionally hide the status bar."
- Release note 55162154 (FB7234376): "You can now use `.toolbarColorScheme(colorScheme, for: .statusBar)` to set a preferred status bar color scheme."
- The statusBarHidden JSON has `deprecated: false` alongside `deprecatedAt "27.2"` (a future SDK version), so it is a scheduled or soft deprecation.
- A skill update should use the new placement behind `if #available(iOS 27, *)` and mention that `statusBarHidden(_:)` is on its way out.

results.corrected_claim:
The API facts are right:
- `struct TabsPickerStyle` and `static var tabs: TabsPickerStyle` exist, introduced 27.0 on iOS, iPadOS, Mac Catalyst, macOS, tvOS and visionOS. There is no watchOS.
- Abstract: "A picker style that presents options as segmented tabs."
- Overview (verbatim, including Apple's typo): "On macOS, this style produces a segmented picker with a visual treatment that distinguishes tab navigation from value selection. On iOS, tvOS, and visionOS, the visual appearance matches that of the standard standard `.segmented` style. On all supported platforms, VoiceOver announces options as tabs."
- Release note 173211711 exists and says the style is "for pickers that represent tab-based navigation and content selection".

The claim about the skill is wrong. patterns/glass-search-field.md line 33 uses `.searchScopes($scope, activation: .onSearchPresentation) { ... }`, which is the system search-scope API, not a segmented Picker. No Apple doc says `pickerStyle(.tabs)` affects `searchScopes`, so it is not a fix for that section. The skill has no `.pickerStyle(.segmented)` anywhere.

The skill's tab-like switchers are custom glass button groups: `segmentedSwitcher` (Sign In / Sign Up) at examples/08-LoginScreen.swift lines 207–209, and the period switcher at examples/09-HealthTodayScreen.swift line 136. TabsPickerStyle could only replace them by giving up the custom glass morph.
results.notes:
Sources: DocC JSON for tabspickerstyle (apple-doc) and the iOS & iPadOS 27 release notes (apple-other).
- Full text of release note 173211711: "The `TabsPickerStyle` style is now available for pickers that represent tab-based navigation and content selection. This style is similar to the `.segmented` style, but VoiceOver reads it as “tabs,” and on macOS it has a distinct visual appearance that distinguishes it from pickers that represent value selection — for example, a text alignment picker in an inspector."
- The finding's quote drops Apple's duplicated word "standard standard" and elides the macOS sentence with "..."; otherwise it is faithful.
- TabsPickerStyle is not in the SwiftUI Updates page's June 2026 bullets. It is documented on the symbol page and in the release notes.

results.corrected_claim:
Verified (verbatim):
- `nonisolated func textInputBorderShape(_ shape: TextInputBorderShape) -> some View`, abstract "Sets the border shape for text input controls in the view hierarchy."
- `struct TextInputBorderShape` with `static var automatic`, `static var capsule` and `static var roundedRectangle`.
- `static var bordered: BorderedTextFieldStyle { get }`, abstract "A text field style with a system-defined border whose shape is determined by the textInputBorderShape(_:) modifier."
- All three are 27.0 on iOS, iPadOS, Mac Catalyst, macOS, tvOS, visionOS and watchOS.
- The doc sample `HStack { TextField("Search", text: $searchText); Button("Go", action: search) }.buttonBorderShape(.capsule).textInputBorderShape(.capsule)` is verbatim.
- `roundedBorder` has deprecatedAt 27.2 on iOS, iPadOS, Mac Catalyst and macOS (not visionOS), with the message "Use `textFieldStyle(.bordered)` with `textInputBorderShape(.roundedRectangle)`".

Wrong: `squareBorder` is macOS-only (introduced 10.15) and does not share that message. Its deprecatedAt 27.2 message is "Use `textFieldStyle(.bordered)` instead. As of macOS 26, text fields no longer have a rectangular border." Release note 173362083 calls both styles "soft deprecated".

The framing is also loose. The skill does already shape fields by hand: examples/06-ChatScreen.swift wraps the TextField at line 74 in `.glassEffect(.regular, in: .capsule)` at line 92, and the 08-LoginScreen.swift fields use `.glassEffect(.regular, in: .rect(cornerRadius: 18))`. What it lacks is the iOS 27 system border-shape API.

The gotcha at line 83 still stands: don't hand-roll a search field from TextField plus `.glassEffect()`, use `.searchable`. Apple's docs don't say that `.bordered` or `textInputBorderShape` render Liquid Glass.
results.notes:
Sources: DocC JSON for view/textinputbordershape(_:), textinputbordershape, textfieldstyle, textfieldstyle/bordered, borderedtextfieldstyle, textfieldstyle/roundedborder and textfieldstyle/squareborder (apple-doc), plus the iOS & iPadOS 27 release notes (apple-other).
- Full text of release note 173362083: "You can now use the `TextInputBorderShape` type to customize the border shape of text input controls like `TextField` with the `textInputBorderShape(_:)` view modifier. The `.squareBorder` and `.roundedBorder` text field styles are soft deprecated — use the new `.bordered` text field style instead."
- Both deprecation entries have `deprecated: false` with `deprecatedAt "27.2"`, which is a future SDK version.
- Any skill code using these APIs needs an iOS 27 availability gate.
